unit.title: The Five Ks, Vaisakhi, and Service

lesson.title: An Introduction to the Five Ks
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: Some Sikhs wear five special items every day, all starting with the letter K. Today we'll meet all five for the first time: the Five Ks.

Kesh is uncut hair. Kangha is a small wooden comb. Kara is a steel bracelet. Kachera is a special undergarment. Kirpan is a small ceremonial sword. Each one is worn as a sign of faith and identity, all the time — not just on special occasions. Can you say all five names in a row?
You just met the Five Ks for the first time! We'll learn more about what each one means in future lessons.

objectives: Name all Five Ks (Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera, Kirpan) in order
Recognize that the Five Ks are worn as signs of faith and identity, all the time
materialsNeeded: Printed 'An Introduction to the Five Ks' worksheet
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce each of the Five Ks by name, one at a time, with a simple one-word description.
2. Practice saying all five names in a row together.
3. Emphasize that these are worn all the time, not just for special occasions.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace each name and its simple description.
5. Close by seeing if the child can recite all five from memory.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just two or three of the five names today, adding the rest in a later review
Ready for more: ask if they know anyone who wears one or more of the Five Ks, and what they've noticed
This is intentionally a simple, K-2-level introduction — a deeper exploration of each K's meaning comes in later grades
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — check that the child can name all five items, even if not yet explaining their deeper meaning.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: A simple, name-level introduction to the Five Ks is the Grade 2 Sikhi course's stated starting point — an age-appropriate first exposure before the deeper meaning-focused treatment in later grades.
